\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{காலாவதியாகு} (kālāvatiyāku)}{காலாவதியாகு (kālāvatiyāku)}]{\ta{காலாவதியாகு} (kālāvatiyāku) — to expire; to lapse}

\label{lesson:TA-C415-kalavatiyaku}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an entrance, then the Tamil for to confiscate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{காலாவதியாகு}}
\textbf{\ta{காலாவதியாகு}} — \emph{kālāvatiyāku} — \textquotedblleft{}to expire; to lapse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{என்} \ta{கடவுச்சீட்டு} \ta{அடுத்த} \ta{மாதம்} \ta{காலாவதியாகும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭu aṭutta mātam kālāvatiyākum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My passport expires next month.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ta{காலாவதியானது}, \emph{kālāvatiyāṉatu}.

Of food or medicine too: \ta{காலாவதியான} \ta{மருந்து}, expired medicine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{காலாவதியாகு}} (\emph{kālāvatiyāku}) is built from \ta{காலாவதி}, \textquotedblleft{}the end of a term\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{kāla}, \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3084), and \emph{avadhi}, \textquotedblleft{}a limit\textquotedblright{}, with \ta{ஆகு}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kālāvatiyāku}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kālāvatiyāku}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭu aṭutta mātam kālāvatiyākum.} — My passport expires next month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an entrance, then the Tamil for to confiscate, then say \emph{kālāvatiyāku} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{காலாவதியாகு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To expire; to lapse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{புதுப்பி} (putuppi)}{புதுப்பி (putuppi)}]{\ta{புதுப்பி} (putuppi) — to renew; to renovate}

\label{lesson:TA-C415-putuppi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to confiscate, then the Tamil for to expire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{புதுப்பி}}
\textbf{\ta{புதுப்பி}} — \emph{putuppi} — \textquotedblleft{}to renew; to renovate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நேற்று} \ta{நான்} \ta{என்} \ta{கடவுச்சீட்டைப்} \ta{புதுப்பித்தேன்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nēṟṟu nāṉ eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭaip putuppittēṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Yesterday I renewed my passport.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{புதுப்பித்தேன்}, \emph{putuppittēṉ}.

Built on \ta{புது}, new: to make new again.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{புதுப்பி}} (\emph{putuppi}) is built from \ta{புது}, \textquotedblleft{}new\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4275), with a verb-making ending: to make new.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{putuppi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{putuppi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nēṟṟu nāṉ eṉ kaṭavuccīṭṭaip putuppittēṉ.} — Yesterday I renewed my passport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to confiscate, then the Tamil for to expire, then say \emph{putuppi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{புதுப்பி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To renew; to renovate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{அலைச்சல்} (alaiccal)}{அலைச்சல் (alaiccal)}]{\ta{அலைச்சல்} (alaiccal) — running around; a weary chase}

\label{lesson:TA-C415-alaiccal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to expire, then the Tamil for to renew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அலைச்சல்}}
\textbf{\ta{அலைச்சல்}} — \emph{alaiccal} — \textquotedblleft{}running around; a weary chase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அந்தச்} \ta{சான்றிதழுக்காக} \ta{எனக்கு} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{வாரம்} \ta{அலைச்சல்} \ta{இருந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{antac cāṉṟitaḻukkāka eṉakku oru vāram alaiccal iruntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Getting that certificate meant a week of running around for me.
\end{quote}

Built on \ta{அலை}, to wander; \ta{வீண்} \ta{அலைச்சல்} is running around for nothing.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{அலைச்சல்}} (\emph{alaiccal}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 240 lists it, \textquotedblleft{}wandering\textquotedblright{}, beside the verb \ta{அலை}, \textquotedblleft{}to move about\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{alaiccal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antac cāṉṟitaḻukkāka eṉakku oru vāram alaiccal iruntatu.} — Getting that certificate meant a week of running around for me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to expire, then the Tamil for to renew, then say \emph{alaiccal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஒப்புகை} (oppukai)}{ஒப்புகை (oppukai)}]{\ta{ஒப்புகை} (oppukai) — an acknowledgement; a receipt slip}

\label{lesson:TA-C415-oppukai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to renew, then the Tamil for running around.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஒப்புகை}}
\textbf{\ta{ஒப்புகை}} — \emph{oppukai} — \textquotedblleft{}an acknowledgement; a receipt slip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அலுவலகம்} \ta{என்} \ta{விண்ணப்பத்துக்கு} \ta{ஒப்புகை} \ta{கொடுத்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aluvalakam eṉ viṇṇappattukku oppukai koṭuttatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The office gave an acknowledgement for my application.
\end{quote}

\ta{ஒப்புகைச்} \ta{சீட்டு} is the slip you keep.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஒப்புகை}} (\emph{oppukai}) is built from \ta{ஒப்பு}, \textquotedblleft{}to agree, to accept\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 924), with the noun ending \emph{-kai}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oppukai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aluvalakam eṉ viṇṇappattukku oppukai koṭuttatu.} — The office gave an acknowledgement for my application.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to renew, then the Tamil for running around, then say \emph{oppukai} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்} (ēṟpāṭu cey)}{ஏற்பாடு செய் (ēṟpāṭu cey)}]{\ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்} (ēṟpāṭu cey) — to arrange; to organise}

\label{lesson:TA-C415-erpatu-cey}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for running around, then the Tamil for an acknowledgement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்}}
\textbf{\ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்}} — \emph{ēṟpāṭu cey} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrange; to organise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அப்பா} \ta{பயணத்துக்கு} \ta{எல்லாம்} \ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்தார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{appā payaṇattukku ellām ēṟpāṭu ceytār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father arranged everything for the trip.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்தேன்}, \emph{ēṟpāṭu ceytēṉ}.

What it is arranged for takes -\ta{க்கு}: \ta{பயணத்துக்கு} \ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்}, to make arrangements for a trip.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்}} (\emph{ēṟpāṭu cey}) joins \ta{ஏற்பாடு}, \textquotedblleft{}an arrangement\textquotedblright{}, which is native Dravidian (DEDR 905), to \ta{செய்}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{appā payaṇattukku ellām ēṟpāṭu ceytār.} — Father arranged everything for the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for running around, then the Tamil for an acknowledgement, then say \emph{ēṟpāṭu cey} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Bends and Slopes to Renewing the Papers}

\label{lesson:TA-R415-review-408-415}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for a curve and a slope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a curve, a slope, an ascent, to overturn, to spin
  \item a pit, a pothole, a level crossing, a shortcut, to get stuck
  \item a pedestrian, a passer-by, a board, to stroll, to cross over
  \item a fault, to stop working, to get dented, to scrape, to bump
  \item a landmark, to lose one's way, to lag behind, to move forward, to move away
  \item a pilot, to make a landing, a wing, customs, immigration
  \item a visa, a border, a checkpoint booth, an entrance, to confiscate
  \item to expire, to renew, running around, an acknowledgement, to arrange
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A curve? (\textbf{\ta{வளைவு}}, \emph{vaḷaivu}.) A slope? (\textbf{\ta{சரிவு}}, \emph{carivu}.) An ascent? (\textbf{\ta{ஏற்றம்}}, \emph{ēṟṟam}.) To overturn? (\textbf{\ta{கவிழ்}}, \emph{kaviḻ}.) To spin? (\textbf{\ta{சுழல்}}, \emph{cuḻal}.) A pit? (\textbf{\ta{குழி}}, \emph{kuḻi}.) A pothole? (\textbf{\ta{பள்ளம்}}, \emph{paḷḷam}.) A level crossing? (\textbf{\ta{கடவை}}, \emph{kaṭavai}.) A shortcut? (\textbf{\ta{குறுக்குவழி}}, \emph{kuṟukkuvaḻi}.) To get stuck? (\textbf{\ta{சிக்கு}}, \emph{cikku}.) A pedestrian? (\textbf{\ta{பாதசாரி}}, \emph{pātacāri}.) A passer-by? (\textbf{\ta{வழிப்போக்கர்}}, \emph{vaḻippōkkar}.) A board? (\textbf{\ta{பலகை}}, \emph{palakai}.) To stroll? (\textbf{\ta{உலாவு}}, \emph{ulāvu}.) To cross over? (\textbf{\ta{தாண்டு}}, \emph{tāṇṭu}.) A fault? (\textbf{\ta{கோளாறு}}, \emph{kōḷāṟu}.) To stop working? (\textbf{\ta{செயலிழ}}, \emph{ceyaliḻa}.) To get dented? (\textbf{\ta{நசுங்கு}}, \emph{nacuṅku}.) To scrape? (\textbf{\ta{உரசு}}, \emph{uracu}.) To bump? (\textbf{\ta{முட்டு}}, \emph{muṭṭu}.) A landmark? (\textbf{\ta{அடையாளம்}}, \emph{aṭaiyāḷam}.) To lose one's way? (\textbf{\ta{வழிதவறு}}, \emph{vaḻitavaṟu}.) To lag behind? (\textbf{\ta{பின்தங்கு}}, \emph{piṉtaṅku}.) To move forward? (\textbf{\ta{முன்னேறு}}, \emph{muṉṉēṟu}.) To move away? (\textbf{\ta{விலகு}}, \emph{vilaku}.) A pilot? (\textbf{\ta{விமானி}}, \emph{vimāṉi}.) To make a landing? (\textbf{\ta{தரையிறங்கு}}, \emph{taraiyiṟaṅku}.) A wing? (\textbf{\ta{இறக்கை}}, \emph{iṟakkai}.) Customs? (\textbf{\ta{சுங்கம்}}, \emph{cuṅkam}.) Immigration? (\textbf{\ta{குடிவரவு}}, \emph{kuṭivaravu}.) A visa? (\textbf{\ta{விசா}}, \emph{vicā}.) A border? (\textbf{\ta{எல்லை}}, \emph{ellai}.) A checkpoint booth? (\textbf{\ta{சாவடி}}, \emph{cāvaṭi}.) An entrance? (\textbf{\ta{நுழைவாயில்}}, \emph{nuḻaivāyil}.) To confiscate? (\textbf{\ta{பறிமுதல்} \ta{செய்}}, \emph{paṟimutal cey}.) To expire? (\textbf{\ta{காலாவதியாகு}}, \emph{kālāvatiyāku}.) To renew? (\textbf{\ta{புதுப்பி}}, \emph{putuppi}.) Running around? (\textbf{\ta{அலைச்சல்}}, \emph{alaiccal}.) An acknowledgement? (\textbf{\ta{ஒப்புகை}}, \emph{oppukai}.) To arrange? (\textbf{\ta{ஏற்பாடு} \ta{செய்}}, \emph{ēṟpāṭu cey}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
